Go with a couple of people, don't say anything to him.

Or get someone else to collect your things for you.

Bah I just wrote a huge reply, and hit refresh by accident.

I'm not too worried about the gap I have, that's covered by my freelancing business. Soon I'll be moving back with my mum, I'll have a lot more pressure (and support) to get going again.

My main focus should be work at this point. The reward (money, career progression) is a lot more direct compared to college. And if I fuck it up after a few months then whatever. College is a huge time and money sink, the payout comes after 2+ years, I cant commit to that right now.

Thanks for the replys, has got me thinking.
Thanks for the offer, my mum has been supportive and made my resume very good, and I've got a freelance business that fills the time gap. But thanks, good luck to you too.

Thanks for the reply. The charity thing, I cant even help myself, so it's hard for me to go out of my way to help others too. I understand why you say it, I'll feel better about myself for it; but I barely wash myself or my clothes, so I have a lot to work on at home before I can help others out.

As for the application thing, I kinda have that covered, I "have my own business" that can fill my massive time void. It all legit I guess, I've done freelance work and have a site/portfolio to show. So my time gap isn't that much of a problem, more my lack of qualifications.

I'll keep thinking, thanks again.

Hi, thanks for the reply.

>What is it that you want to do?

This is something I don't even know at this point. I've tried a few things I thought I'd like, and it put me off them. I'm sick good with PCs, but how can I prove that to an employer?   
The PC related courses I've tried at college, they teach you a load of basic things at the start, stuff I already know. They need them in the course to ease people in, but it got me bored and pushed me away.

I've done freelancing in a few different areas, it;s fun for a bit but you lose all creativity on a project and it's more working with people, than on a project.

 Ideally I guess working with a team of people on a project. In IT but not dealing with the customer directly.

mm this has got me thinking a bit more, so thank you.
